So, we need to modify these files after renaming the two files.Rename the files: Use mv command to rename current_prompt.yaml to prompt.yaml and current_prompt.md to prompt.md.Modify dependencies:In createPrompt.js, replace the instance of current_prompt.yaml with prompt.yaml.In processPrompt.js, replace the instance of current_prompt.md with prompt.md.To prevent any breakages in the application, test the application thoroughly after making these changes.Shell Script[CODE_BLOCK_0]NotePlease run this script from the root directory of your project.Make sure you have a backup of your project or your project is under version control like git before running this script, to prevent any accidental loss of data or work.Remember to test the application thoroughly after running this script to ensure everything is still working as expected.

#!/bin/bash

# Step 1: Rename files
mv ./current_prompt.yaml ./prompt.yaml
mv ./current_prompt.md ./prompt.md

# Step 2: Update dependencies
sed -i 's/current_prompt\.yaml/prompt.yaml/g' ./src/prompt/createPrompt.js
sed -i 's/current_prompt\.md/prompt.md/g' ./src/prompt/processPrompt.js

echo "Files renamed and dependencies updated successfully."

conversations.answer: I apologize for the confusion. The issue is due to a difference in the implementation of the sed command between GNU/Linux and BSD/OSX.The -i option in the sed command is used to make changes in-place in the file. In GNU/Linux, you can use sed -i 's/foo/bar/' filename but in BSD/OSX, you need to provide an extension for the backup file like so sed -i '' -e 's/foo/bar/' filename.Here is the modified script which should work on BSD/OSX systems:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Again, please make sure you have a backup of your project or your project is under version control like git before running this script. Test the application thoroughly after running this script to ensure everything is still working as expected.
